analysis.explanation: The Random Forest classified this binary as malware with probability 1.0000, and all 20 top SHAP features push toward cryptojacking (+0.0069 to +0.0170). The n-grams fall into three clusters typical of hash-based proof-of-work mining code. (1) SSE2 vector register manipulation: PXOR MOVAPS (+0.01704), PXOR PXOR (+0.01379), PXOR MOVDQA (+0.01332), MOVDQA PXOR (+0.00873), LEA MOVDQA (+0.00944), PADDQ MOVDQA (+0.00715), LEA PXOR (+0.00711), MOVQ PUNPCKLQDQ (+0.01013), MOVHLPS MOVQ (+0.01142), ADD MOVQ (+0.00946) and CALL MOVQ (+0.00865). These suggest 128-bit XOR, 64-bit add and lane packing/unpacking of the kind used in memory-hard hashing state mixing (for example CryptoNight-style AES/Keccak/Blake-like state handling). (2) Rotate and shift bit-mixing: XOR ROL (+0.01090), MOV ROL (+0.00900), ROL ROR (+0.00887), ADD ROR (+0.00846), ROL ADD (+0.00725), ROL MOV (+0.00694) and SHL OR (+0.00864). These are ARX-style primitives common in hash functions and ciphers. (3) Multi-precision arithmetic: SUB ADC (+0.01014) and DIV MUL (+0.00773), consistent with 128-bit or big-number math in hashing or difficulty and nonce calculations. The consistent direction of SHAP values, the high frequency of the vector n-grams (MOVQ PUNPCKLQDQ at 0.0070, PXOR MOVDQA at 0.0019) and the absence of any benign-leaning features support a high-confidence call. The evidence is limited to mnemonic n-grams with no function names or API calls, so it indicates mining-style compute kernels rather than proving a specific miner family. Vector and rotate-heavy code can also appear in legitimate crypto libraries, which tempers the score slightly.

evidence_analysis.assessment: Strongest feature. SSE XOR followed by an aligned vector move is characteristic of vectorized state mixing in hash and cipher rounds used by miners.
Consecutive 128-bit XORs indicate dense bitwise mixing, typical of hashing inner loops.
XOR combined with aligned 128-bit loads and stores suggests block-wise processing of scratchpad or state data.
High-to-low lane moves and 64-bit extraction are used when handling 128-bit state halves in hash and multiplication steps.
XOR plus rotate is a core ARX primitive in hash and cipher functions such as those used in PoW algorithms.
Subtract and add-with-carry indicates multi-word arithmetic, consistent with big-number or 128-bit math.
Frequent (0.0070) packing of two 64-bit values into a vector register, a hallmark of vectorized 64-bit hash state handling.
Scalar addition feeding 64-bit vector moves points to mixing between scalar and SIMD computation paths.
Address computation followed by aligned vector load or store suggests indexed access to large buffers such as scratchpads.
Rotation of freshly loaded values is consistent with hash round functions.
Opposing rotations are common in SHA/Blake/Keccak-style bit diffusion.
Load then XOR of vector data, the mirror of PXOR MOVDQA, reinforcing a vectorized XOR-mixing loop.
A call followed by a 64-bit vector move suggests helper routines returning or handling 64-bit hash values. Weaker in isolation.
Shift-and-combine is used for bit packing and manual rotation; moderately common in hashing but not specific.
Add then rotate is a classic ARX round step.
Very rare (0.000004) but strongly weighted; suggests wide-integer arithmetic such as modular or difficulty calculations.
Rotate then add is another ARX pattern consistent with hash compression functions.
Packed 64-bit addition on vector state indicates SIMD arithmetic in a compute kernel.
Address generation followed by vector XOR suggests XOR against indexed memory, such as scratchpad lookups.
Rotate followed by a move fits an unrolled round function storing intermediate results.

key_indicators: Dense SSE2 XOR/MOVDQA/MOVAPS patterns consistent with vectorized hash state mixing
Multiple rotate-based ARX n-grams (XOR ROL, ROL ROR, ADD ROR, ROL ADD)
MOVQ/PUNPCKLQDQ/MOVHLPS 64-bit lane manipulation typical of PoW hashing kernels
Multi-precision arithmetic patterns (SUB ADC, DIV MUL)
All 20 top SHAP features push toward cryptojacking, with RF probability 1.0000
analysis.recommended_action: Treat as a probable cryptominer. Run it in a sandbox and check for mining pool connections, Stratum protocol traffic, sustained high CPU usage and persistence mechanisms. Statically locate the functions containing the PXOR/MOVDQA and ROL/ROR loops to identify the hash algorithm and any embedded wallet or pool configuration. Isolate affected hosts and block related network indicators.
